title: How do you migrate a live workflow from synchronous REST to Kafka without a flag-day cutover: let both models coexist, define which is authoritative at each stage, use shadow/dual processing + idempotent consumers + feature flags to validate the event path, then transfer ownership gradually without losing or duplicating business operations?
shortTitle: How do you migrate a live workflow from synchronous REST to Kafka without a flag-day cutover
keyPoints: A flag-day cutover is unacceptable for a live financial workflow because any bug means lost or duplicated money with no safe rollback.
Stage 1: coexistence with REST authoritative; publish Kafka events via outbox alongside the existing REST path.
Stage 2: shadow processing with an idempotent consumer building a parallel state; reconcile daily to validate equivalence.
Stage 3: feature flags control which path is authoritative per segment, starting with internal accounts then ramping to 1%, 10%, 50%, 100%.
Stage 4: decommission the old REST path only after the event path has been fully authoritative and equivalent for a sustained period.
Idempotency guarantees no duplication, the outbox guarantees no loss, reconciliation gives confidence, and the feature flag is the control surface.
The ability to roll back instantly at every stage is the whole point of avoiding a flag day.

s1_definition.oneliner: Run both paths together with the old one authoritative, shadow-validate the Kafka path with idempotent consumers and feature flags, then ramp ownership gradually and decommission only after the event path proves equivalent.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Flag-day cutover** – Switching everything at once at midnight; unacceptable for live financial workflows because bugs mean lost or duplicated money.
- **Coexistence** – Both REST and Kafka paths run simultaneously; the old path remains the source of truth during validation.
- **Shadow processing** – A new consumer applies events into a parallel copy of state without affecting real customers; a reconciler compares outcomes.
- **Feature flags** – Control which path is authoritative per segment, enabling gradual ramp from 0% to 100% with instant rollback.
- **Reconciliation** – Automated comparison of shadow and authoritative outcomes to prove equivalence under production load.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India wants to switch from processing transfers at the old manual counter to a new automated conveyor. They run both at once: the old counter still officially processes every transfer, while the new conveyor quietly processes a copy and the staff compare results every evening. Once the conveyor matches the counter perfectly for weeks, they let it handle 10% of real transfers, then 50%, then all, and finally retire the counter. A unique stamp on each slip ensures no transfer is done twice while both run.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A flag-day cutover is unacceptable for a live financial workflow because if anything is wrong you have already lost or duplicated money with no safe rollback. Instead, migrate as a sequence of reversible stages where the synchronous REST path and the new Kafka event path coexist and you always know which one is authoritative.

The stages are concrete. First, coexistence: REST stays authoritative while you publish Kafka events via a transactional outbox. Second, shadow processing: an idempotent consumer builds a parallel state and a reconciler compares outcomes daily. Third, feature flags ramp authority from internal accounts to 1% to 100% of real traffic, with instant rollback at every step. Fourth, decommission the old path only after the event path has been fully authoritative and clean for weeks.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj moved the transfer workflow this way. REST stayed authoritative while events flowed via an outbox. A shadow consumer built a shadow ledger, and nightly reconciliation proved equivalence including absorbing duplicate deliveries. The feature flag ramped from internal accounts to 1% over two weeks, with the ability to flip back instantly, and only after 100% clean for a month did they remove the old path.

Remember one sentence: avoid a flag day by running both paths with the old one authoritative, shadow-validate with idempotent consumers and reconciliation, then use feature flags to ramp authority gradually with instant rollback, so ownership transfers without ever losing or duplicating a business operation.
